reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about low lattice distortion and dislocation resistance in CoCrFeNiTi, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address this alloy system or its deformation mechanisms. E1 discusses a phase transformation in CrCoNi, and E2 describes boride precipitation at grain boundaries in HfMoNbTaTiZr, neither of which supports the key premises about CoCrFeNiTi's solid-solution state or the proposed nanoscale obstacle mechanism.
premises: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has low lattice distortion and thus low dislocation resistance
Low dislocation resistance enables easy dislocation motion on many slip systems, limiting work hardening and strength
Introducing nanoscale precipitates or short-range order creates obstacles that impede dislocation motion
These obstacles increase the stress required for dislocation nucleation and glide, raising hardness and yield strength
The cited evidence supports the role of lattice distortion and precipitates in dislocation-mediated strengthening
